subject: FinBridge: request for incident-time logs and redaction workflow
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finbridge.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finbridge.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in 5xx / latency — need logs for executive review

Grace —

We observed a sustained spike in 5xx errors and end-to-end latency from ~08:45–09:30 PDT this morning for requests routed to 'gptx-4-highmem' for our production tenant (FinBridge prod). Error rates were ~6% and p95 latency doubled. Our execs want a short packet of evidence for an internal review this afternoon. Can you confirm whether Redwood retains request/response traces and what the timeline is for pulling a verifiable log bundle? We need:
- request IDs (we sampled ff3a7b, c21d9b)
- raw request timestamps and status codes
- any server-side error stack traces and telemetry

Also let me know if you can provide a redacted bundle (remove user PII) or whether we need to accept hashed manifests instead. Adding security@finbridge.com to the thread.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Platform Operations, FinBridge
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finbridge.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx / latency — need logs for executive review

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the sample IDs. We're marking the relevant data on legal hold and will preserve all incident artifacts immediately. Quick items:

1) Scope: can you confirm the exact customer tenant (you said FinBridge prod) and the time window you want us to preserve (we'll start with 08:30–10:00 PDT unless you tell us otherwise).
2) Output format: do you want full raw request/response bodies (we'll need a formal redaction agreement) or a redaction-ready bundle (we create a redacted extract and also provide signed hashes of the originals)?
3) Urgency: do you need an evidence packet for a 3pm PDT exec call today? We can produce a preliminary manifest + sampled artifacts by then; full bundle will take longer depending on redaction.

For transparency I'm looping engineering and security to confirm what logs exist and how we'll handle chain-of-custody.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@finbridge.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx / latency — need logs for executive review

Alex / Grace — technical summary of what we can pull immediately (short version):

- Ingress logs: timestamp, request_id, tenant_id, route, response_code, duration, node_id, and truncated header hashes. These are available for 30 days by default.
- Runtime traces: per-request error traces and stack snippets (no full model token stream by default). Detailed traces are present only when debug-tracing was enabled; not all requests will have full payloads.
- Serving telemetry: per-shard CPU/GPU utilization, queue depths, batching metrics and KV cache hit stats (these are aggregated metrics).
- Persistent artifacts: stored debug traces and system logs (these can be kept longer under legal hold).
- What we do NOT by default retain: complete plaintext user inputs/responses in full fidelity unless a customer opt-in (debug) was enabled.

We can:
1) Freeze the storage locations for the 08:30–10:00 PDT window and generate a signed manifest of files preserved (SHA256 checksums).
2) Produce a redaction workflow: create a copy, run token-level PII filter (configurable), output a redacted bundle and a separate checksum+signature of the original files for chain-of-custody.

If you need immediate artifacts for the 3pm call, tell us which sample request_ids you want first (you provided two — we'll start there).

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finbridge.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 12:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx / latency — need logs for executive review

Alex / Grace — from a security & compliance perspective:

- Default retention: raw ingress metadata + response codes = 30 days; debug traces (when enabled) are retained 90 days.
- Legal hold: we will extend retention to 365 days for the files preserved under this incident if requested by FinBridge compliance.
- Chain of custody: we provide a signed manifest (SHA256) and a tamper-evident bundle delivered over our secure transfer (S3 presigned link with IP restrictions) or encrypted SFTP.
- PII redaction: we will apply the agreed token-level filters. We recommend the customer supply an allow-list/deny-list as part of redaction acceptance criteria.
- Audit artifacts: we can include per-file checksums, internal access log snapshot (who accessed the files) and a short notarization statement from Redwood security. Note: redaction is irreversible for the redacted bundle; we will keep originals under legal hold if you request it.

Proposed next steps:
1) FinBridge confirms window and redaction rules.
2) Redwood produces a signed manifest + preliminary sample artifacts (2–3 requests) by 3pm PDT.
3) Redwood and FinBridge agree on delivery method and legal hold duration.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finbridge.com>, security@finbridge.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx / latency — need logs for executive review

Alex / FinBridge security —

Per Marcus and Rishi, here's our plan and what we'll deliver for the 3pm PDT window:
- Preservation: we've frozen 08:30–10:00 PDT and created a read-only copy.
- Preliminary deliverable (by 3pm PDT): signed manifest (redwood_filtered_logs_manifest.txt), a 3-request sample bundle with PII redacted per token filter (sample IDs: ff3a7b, c21d9b, 9d7f2a) and an incident_summary.csv (high-level metrics: counts, p95, p99, node errors).
- Final deliverable (48–72 hrs): full redaction-run bundle + chain-of-custody bundle; or, if you want originals preserved offsite, we will apply legal hold and provide signed hashes.

Attachment: incident_summary.csv (stub) — includes counts and timing for the window.

Please confirm: 1) confirm 08:30–10:00 PDT; 2) confirm that FinBridge requires PII removal (yes/no) and any deny-list items; 3) whether FinBridge will accept hashed originals + redacted bundle or wants originals transferred under an NDA/legal request.

If you confirm now we'll proceed and have the manifest + samples at 3pm.

—Grace
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finbridge.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finbridge.com, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx / latency — need logs for executive review

Grace — thanks for the quick action. Apologies for the delay in confirming: FinBridge legal wants originals preserved (hash+manifest) but will accept a redacted bundle for the exec packet. Two asks before we close the loop:

1) Please include an access-log snapshot showing which Redwood employees accessed preserved artifacts and when (we need that for our audit).
2) We'd like a written statement that debug traces do not include persistent model-secret material or raw KV cache content; confirm what (if anything) in the preserved artifacts could contain customer-sensitive tokens so we can scope redaction.

If you can provide the manifest + sample redacted bundle and the access-log snapshot, we'll confirm the legal hold length (likely 1 year). Also opening a parallel request for SLA credit assessment with Monica.

Thanks —
Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Platform Operations, FinBridge
